# WF-05 · Premium Motion Editing

## Complete operating codex · foundation v1.0

**User policy locked 15 October 2026:** V5 clean editorial direction + accepted V6 depth/motion/transition/sound. **No V6 bottom caption pills or active-word lower strip by default.**

This is a source-backed production library: creative DNA, metaphors, motion, typography, narration, cleanup, engineering, QA, recovery and cross-platform operation. Historical source/evidence is preserved alongside the new reusable approved profile.

No newly rendered full-length combined-policy master is claimed. Technical validity, creative fidelity and user acceptance are distinct.

# 01 · Identity, approval and the quality contract

## One style, one identity

**WF-05 · Premium Motion Editing** is a distinct permanent style in Monarch Studio. Its stable repository identity is `premium-motion-editing`; its entry command is `MOTIONGO <topic or reference>`. `WF-05`, `WF5` and the full name are aliases, not new workflows. The existing user-created Drive folder is reused. Do not create another WF-05 merely because a new chat starts.

The style is an editorial motion argument: ideas become tangible subjects, objects and relationships; those objects actually change over time; concise kinetic type directs attention; voice determines the semantic edit; restrained sound accents make actions feel intentional. A busy filter stack is not the definition of premium.

## Binding user decision — 15 October 2026

The user approved the V5-level clean direction and the non-caption improvements made in V6, but explicitly called V6's **lower caption treatment** bad. This is a component-level decision, not a rejection of every V6 improvement and not permission to keep the pill strip because technical tests passed.

The production default therefore combines:

- V5-like clean composition and integrated editorial hierarchy;
- accepted V6 near/far depth motion, perspective/extruded title entrances, short transition grammar and sound accents;
- **no V6 bottom caption pills and no active-word lower strip**;
- optional separate SRT for accessibility; plain V5-like subtitle text only when the brief explicitly requests it.

“Bottom captions rejected” does **not** ban an integrated headline placed below the subject. `BHAAG NAHI`, `AI SHORTCUTS`, `MUSCLES` and a closing question can belong in the lower part of a deliberate composition. The rejected thing is the separate recurring sentence-pill UI competing with that composition.

`data/approved-profile.json` is the machine-readable decision. `records/USER_REQUEST_20261015.txt` preserves the exact visible request. If historical V6 code disagrees, the latest policy wins. Originals remain unchanged as evidence. A new full-length combined-policy master was **not** rendered as part of this foundation; do not label V6 itself the fully approved default.

## Acceptance is not a slogan

A future project must demonstrate actual motion, readable hierarchy, correct meaning, safe subject edges, voice/picture alignment, clean branding, decodable export and recoverable delivery. The foundation preserves a tested reference level and executable guards; it cannot guarantee every future model output will be perfect. Reuse the production grammar, not the old Einstein story for an unrelated topic.

## Separation from the rest of the studio

WF-01's stickman/SHADE engine, WF-03's noir world, WF-04's locked personal hero and other folders remain separate. Do not import a Monarch face, crown finale, logo or unrelated workflow trigger by habit. Shared assets require explicit casting and appropriate rights. A folder visible in Drive does not prove that its full implementation exists in this checkout.

# 02 · Visual DNA and composition

## The observed world

The reference and retained V5/V6 direction use a luminous pale-lavender center, deeper periwinkle edges and subtle paper/linen texture. Subjects are grayscale or violet-tinted photographic cut-outs and impossible-but-readable object assemblies. Ground shadows, foreshortening, scale and orbital marks make the stage feel dimensional. Large condensed ink headlines contrast with small italic connectors.

The baseline ink is RGB **30, 22, 59**. V6's secondary violet is **76, 45, 113**; a depth-shadow purple is **112, 91, 173**. These are observed implementation values, not a mandate to tint every pixel identically. Preserve tonal hierarchy: the subject and the claim must win over grain, glows and decorative lines.

## Hierarchy before effects

1. Decide what the viewer must understand in this beat.
2. Give that beat one dominant subject or object relation.
3. Place the main word/claim where the subject leaves readable space.
4. Add connectors only when they improve meaning.
5. Use secondary props to clarify the metaphor, not to fill empty space.
6. Let movement hand attention from voice to subject to keyword.

Negative space is useful. Do not cover every quiet area with a label. Do not put a permanent UI band at the bottom simply because subtitles are available. A title can live above, below or beside the hero; its placement follows the composition, not a single fixed paragraph box.

## Subject integrity

Faces, hands, fingers, bow/violin strings, crutch tips, shoe silhouettes, hanging ropes and shadow contact points are protected details. Missing pale highlights are not acceptable “background cleanup.” Depth boundaries belong in empty background margins. A dark bag may share the exact purple of the font: color alone is not semantic segmentation.

Keep camera and subject perspective coherent. A ground shadow should stay attached to its subject; an orbit's rear segment should read behind the figure, not cut randomly through the face. A visual may be surreal while its local spatial logic stays clear.

## What is flexible and what is locked

Locked: actual temporal motion, clean editorial hierarchy, concept-led imagery, natural narration pace unless explicitly changed, no accidental social branding, current caption policy, truthful production claims.

Flexible with deliberate review: metaphor, subject, narrative setting, secondary objects, shot length, palette variants, camera direction, transition selection and emphasis words. The lavender family is the default reference, not an excuse to repeat the same props forever. A different format or writing system needs a tested adapter, not silent stretching or missing glyphs.

## Do not confuse three things

A still image with a whole-frame zoom is camera movement. Independently changing objects/layers or native moving footage provide subject motion. Newly modeled and animated geometry is actual 3D production. This case used supplied moving footage plus 2.5D compositing and 3D-style type; it did not reconstruct Einstein or the vehicles as new 3D models.

# 03 · Reference inspection, story and accurate adaptation

## Inspect first, not after rendering

Recover the supplied reference and any prior outputs before generating replacements. Read metadata, save source IDs/hashes, inspect the complete sequence with contact sheets, then inspect dense frames around transitions, moving labels and tag locations. A file name or a prior agent's summary is not visual evidence.

For this case the recovered reference was 720×1282 at 30 fps; the 720×1280 working stage removed one pixel from top and bottom. The original social ending was excluded after source time 51.64s. Full duration and container/audio duration can differ slightly; do not invent a frame count from an approximate player display.

Build an inspection ledger: source time, subject, object state, camera behavior, typography region, tag corner, transition, and likely edit boundary. Sparse samples can tell you the style; they cannot certify the exact cut. The watch-to-flow and flow-to-car boundaries required denser inspection.

## Argument spine of the case

The supplied story moves from an Einstein/gravity anecdote to a musical change of mental mode, to a claim about flow and AI shortcuts; it then uses cars versus running as an analogy for chosen effort, extends that analogy to the brain, introduces “creative inflation,” contrasts efficiency and talent, and closes on people paying to carry heavy sandbags and what that suggests about art.

That structure is an argument, not a list of decorative nouns. Each visual performs a job: establish pressure, change state, contrast convenience with practice, show divergence, then leave an unresolved consequence. The shot map in the case project records all fourteen observed mechanisms.

## Translation method

Preserve meaning, causality, emphasis and tone in easy Urdu-English. Keep useful terms such as flow state, AI shortcuts, efficiency and creative inflation where they are clearer than a forced substitute. Break spoken lines at meaningful clauses. Roman Urdu on-screen wording should be short enough to read while watching motion.

Do not change the argument merely to fit an English source duration. Do not shrink a whole translated paragraph to microscopic text. Do not equate a caption transcript with certified word-by-word speech recognition. The selected audio files remain the spoken authority; the recorded Roman Urdu phrases are the on-screen script.

## Fact and metaphor boundaries

The Einstein/Mozart anecdote was adapted from the supplied reference, not independently verified history. The opening “Ek mashhoor kahani” preserves that boundary. Claims about shortcuts, creativity and talent are the reference's rhetoric; a visual metaphor is not evidence of a scientific causal law.

For a new topic, make a claim ledger: assertion, source or user-provided premise, confidence, and wording. Mark uncertain anecdotes as stories. Do not fabricate dates, quotes, studies, footage provenance or scientific certainty. Avoid using body shape or disability imagery as proof of laziness, worth or cognitive ability.

## Reuse scope

If the task is a reference adaptation, preserve the reference's essential motion grammar and argument. If the task is a new production, create a new topic-specific argument and matching motion assets. An Einstein replay is not a completed new video about a different topic simply because its title changed.

# 04 · Creative engine, concepts and metaphor grammar

## Convert an idea into a visual mechanism

Use this chain: **abstract claim → concrete subject/object → relationship → action/state change → consequence → attention hand-off**.

A good metaphor can be understood in one glance and becomes more meaningful through motion. “Efficiency rises while talent falls” is stronger as two opposing vertical systems than as two unrelated pictures. “Chosen resistance” is clearer when a carried weight visibly affects effort than when a bag sits on a static slide.

For every proposed shot, answer: What changes? Why does it change? What does the change mean? Which word should the viewer hear/see at that moment? What would make the metaphor misleading? If the only answer is “the camera zooms,” the scene needs actual subject/layer motion or a different concept.

## Internal concept selection

Develop at least three feasible concepts internally when the brief is open. Score argument fit, one-glance clarity, causal readability, independent-motion potential, novelty relative to the style's prior projects, and asset/rights feasibility. Select a concept because it serves the message, not because it adds the most effects.

Record rejected concepts and why. A new chat should not waste time rediscovering that an option is visually confusing, legally unavailable or impossible with the current toolchain. Use `brain/registry.json` to avoid repeating the same prop/world/device combination for every subject.

## Useful operations

- **Scale contrast:** make the operative object unusually large while preserving a readable relationship to the person.
- **Materialization:** give an abstract noun a tangible state: burning, deflating, being supported, becoming heavy, or rising.
- **Opposed vectors:** two systems move in different directions so the trade-off is visible.
- **Functional substitution:** place a machine where a human function would be, while keeping the critique about behavior rather than a person's worth.
- **Voluntary difficulty:** show a person choosing resistance despite access to convenience.
- **Compression:** combine time, practice and thought in one legible assembly rather than adding several slides.
- **Delayed consequence:** resolve the image but leave a meaningful question, not an unrelated logo card.

## Novelty without random surrealism

Surprise must still be interpretable. Limit the number of competing actions. Keep one foreground idea dominant. A viewer should not need to decode five unrelated symbols before hearing the next sentence. New idea seeds in `data/metaphor-bank.json` are explicitly labeled as suggestions, not previously rendered projects.

Novelty is not achieved by changing only a color or replacing Einstein's face. For a new subject, change the conceptual mechanism, setting or relationship while retaining the quality grammar. Reuse engineering components—camera maps, typography fitting, codecs, recovery—not somebody else's entire argument by accident.

## Motion planning worksheet

For each beat, specify: primary subject; secondary props; independent action; near/far depth plateau; protected details; start/hold/exit; emphasis word; transition reason; narration interval; sound event; and evidence of actual motion. These fields belong in `shot-plan.csv` before full export. A plan without assets remains a plan, not a delivered animation.

# 05 · Motion, depth and transitions

## Preserve motion before adding motion

The repair retained changing reference frames in fourteen prepared clips. The clip is sampled across time and retimed to the spoken beat. New camera motion does not replace native changes of orientation, stride, prop position or gesture. The source-only motion diagnostic runs before the new captions; animated text cannot make a still-image source pass the creative review.

Frame blending provides a lightweight interpolation between adjacent native frames. It can create ghosting during fast action. Inspect those moments; consider safer source trims or a separately tested interpolation method rather than pretending every blended frame is perfect. The case retained some intentional source motion-blur/grid treatments.

## Near/far 2.5D maps

V6 introduced independent near/far inverse maps, a modest dolly/yaw/roll and gentle far-plane softening. Crucially, it did not key out pale foreground pixels. A constant-depth plateau covers the complete subject cluster, and feathering happens in empty paper margins. A boundary through a face, hand, hair or string can deform it.

Historical case plateau rectangles and per-shot zoom strengths remain in the unchanged V6 module. The reusable module accepts a normalized rectangle and camera parameters from each new shot. Do not carry the old brain/runner geometry into a different project by scene number.

Observed V6 strengths ranged roughly 0.025–0.09; its case roll amplitude was 0.65 degrees and far-focus sigma 0.8. These are restrained implementation values, not universal aesthetic commandments. Check frame edges and subject proportions at the strongest transform, not only at rest.

## Three short transition treatments

**Depth push, around 0.25s:** a conceptual escalation or move into a state. It briefly changes scale/roll and applies restrained radial blur.

**Diagonal whip, around 0.25s:** a fast causal or analogy hand-off. Translation and directional blur connect two moving scenes. Do not prolong it until both scenes become illegible.

**Feathered directional cut, around 0.22s:** a clean hand-off without a full white flash. It should feel like a designed change, not a long slideshow dissolve.

Select a transition for a reason. Blindly alternating every effect is not direction. The historical V6 renderer cycles treatments as an implementation detail; the reusable shot manifest lets the editor choose deliberately.

## Typography as a separate plane

Titles can enter with a brief perspective yaw and extrusion, then settle into a readable hold. The case used a 0.34s entry and stronger relief in V6. The main word must stay readable for most of its display time. Endless distortion, bouncing every syllable or effect-driven overlap with a face is not premium.

## Non-negotiable review

Review entry, settled pose, strongest transform and exit. Inspect foreground edges, shadows, strings, shoes, source-mask boundaries and type collisions. Use several closely spaced frames around known problems. A midpoint-only contact sheet missed defects in the original repair; dense inspection found them.

# 06 · Typography and the rejected caption treatment

## The approved hierarchy

The scene carries the idea. Type highlights its meaning. Use a short kicker, a dominant condensed word or phrase, and a small connective line only when needed. Anton supplies the headline weight; Barlow Condensed Medium/Medium Italic supplies connectors and optional plain text. Font licenses are bundled.

Observed case headline sizes were approximately 64–124 at a 720×1280 design base, rendered at 1.5× for the 1080×1920 output. These numbers are not a license to force every phrase into one line. Fit the word count and line breaks to a readable minimum. The reusable compositor refuses unreadable overflow rather than shrinking indefinitely.

Top, bottom and side anchors are valid when the subject leaves room. The case needed a higher brain heading and careful separation around the violinist's feet and final pen nibs. New projects must declare their own geometry and review collisions instead of copying those special cases blindly.

## Latest user correction

V6 added a recurring dark rounded caption pill and active-word highlight at the bottom. The user explicitly rejected that treatment while accepting the other improvements. Therefore the production module has **no pill/word-strip renderer**. Its default is integrated scene type, with the separate subtitle overlay off.

A V5-like plain subtitle line is available only when requested in the brief and explicitly acknowledged by `plain_subtitles_requested=true`. It has no box, no pill and no active-word highlighting. A separate SRT may be delivered without burning an unwanted UI band into the picture.

## Avoid the common mistakes

- Do not overlay a full translated paragraph at a tiny size.
- Do not leave the old English behind and add a second competing text layer.
- Do not fill every lower-third gap with a permanent caption bar.
- Do not treat “newest version” as “approved version.” V6's technical pass did not override user feedback.
- Do not ban integrated lower-positioned headlines just because bottom caption pills were rejected.
- Do not claim proportional word highlighting is exact ASR alignment.

## Language capability

This reusable adapter is tested for Latin/Roman Urdu typography. Actual Urdu script requires a tested RTL/shaping/font backend. Do not render broken glyphs or microscopic substitutes and call it accurate localization. Keep phonetic clarity and meaning in the audio independent of the display script.

## Regression contract

Tests must reject `pill`, `karaoke`, `word_highlight`, `caption_pills=true` and `word_highlighting=true` in the approved production profile. They must allow normal bottom-positioned integrated titles. Tests must also ensure a new project does not copy Einstein text/audio and that a second project cannot inherit cached typography from the first.

# 07 · Narration, rhythm and sound

## Preserve selected work

The repair recovered the exact nine previously selected MP3 clips from immutable Git source and verified their hashes. It did not ask for another voice selection or synthesize new narration merely because local render caches were missing. V5 and V6 use natural 1.0× speech pace.

For a new script, do not reuse the old Einstein words. Reuse a voice preference/reference where appropriate, but obey the current speech tool's registration requirements. Session voice IDs are not guaranteed portable across chats. Existing audio files are durable assets; a remembered tool ID is not the audio itself.

## Let the voice establish the edit

Measure actual decoded audio. In the case, source clips were decoded to 48kHz mono for timing, leading/trailing quiet was tightened with small safety margins, and durations were rounded to the 30fps frame grid by adding quiet—not by cutting phonemes. Clip starts, trims and ends are preserved in each timeline.

The observed analysis used 10ms RMS windows, a 0.012 activity threshold, approximately 65ms leading margin and 130ms trailing margin. Those values are a case recipe, not a universal voice detector. Quiet consonants and breath require listening/inspection; never blindly reuse a threshold on a different recording.

Retiming the picture per semantic beat is preferable to global voice speed-up merely to match an English video's length. The case became 63.1 seconds while preserving the natural dub. The two clocks, violin/flow transitions, car/runner contrast and closing argument must follow the sentence that gives them meaning.

## Sound accents, not audio clutter

The case used a restrained procedural tonal floor, filtered-noise cut accents and small type taps. V6 added quiet clock/chalk/running cues and a closing rise. These are sound-design accents, **not** a claimed recording of Mozart. Use licensed/provided music if actual music is required; do not pretend a spoken-word synthesis tool sings or produces orchestral music.

Prioritize intelligible narration. Keep accents below dialogue, use pan sparingly, retain headroom and inspect final encoded audio. Loudness normalization does not fix a mistranslated script, distorted source or wrongly timed effect.

## Export and measurement

The case mix targeted FFmpeg loudnorm I=-16, TP=-1.5, LRA=9 and encoded AAC stereo at 192kbps / 48kHz. Decoded sample peaks were -1.52dBFS for V5 and -1.97dBFS for V6; both had roughly -19.57dBFS RMS. **RMS is not integrated LUFS, and sample peak is not automatically true peak.** State exactly which measurement was made.

Earlier QA decoded, timed and level-checked the output; it did not claim an independent human listening pass. Preserve that scope honestly. Record any final listening review actually performed rather than filling an approval field from intention.

# 08 · Cleaning flattened references without damaging subjects

## Why localization is more than a new audio track

V4 retained old English typography, social tags and the Instagram end card, while the Urdu overlay was too small. Replacing audio alone did not meet the request. The repair localized the picture: it cleaned old glyphs/tags, rebuilt integrated type and excluded the social ending.

## The rejected approaches

Large Telea inpainting areas produced cloudy paper patches. A background-key/matte experiment removed pale hair, bulb highlights and thin details because their colors resembled the stage. Both were rejected rather than quietly called improvements. The rejected `matte.py` remains in the historical V5 source as evidence, not as the approved engine.

## The retained case method

Use shot-aware text regions, identify the intended ink, dilate enough to cover antialiasing, and apply Navier–Stokes inpainting. Review background texture after cleanup. This is restoration of flattened source pixels, not magical recovery of what was hidden by lettering; some texture softening remains a real limitation.

Detect the active Instagram icon position by template matching before masking its associated handle. The reference alternated between upper-right and lower-left. Erasing both locations in every shot damaged the hanging stone in the talent scene, where no lower-left tag was present. Observed true matches were approximately 0.85–0.997, versus about 0.10–0.21 for empty regions; the implementation used a case-specific threshold.

## Moving typography requires moving masks

The year, running-shoe heading and other text moved during entry. Settled-frame rectangles left partial letters. The watch/flow transition also arrived earlier than a sparse sample suggested. Inspect dense source frames and encode reviews around those boundaries.

The runner is the clearest caution: an early broad lower mask cut low-positioned shoes; a later ramp preserved shoes but missed the first rows of SPRINT. V6's targeted fix kept early shoes and cleaned the full lower title after the source runner rose, at approximately 25.70s. This is a **case coordinate/time**, not a universal rule for every runner.

Dark-purple sandbags could be mistaken for ink. Connected-component size/location protected the subject. Pale crutches, reflective metal, strings and hair need different caution. Do not convert a color heuristic into a claim that the machine understands an object.

## Transfer to a new project

The historical cleaner is fully preserved, but its coordinates are tied to this source. A new reference needs its own inspection and masks. Stage prepared, clean motion clips for the reusable compositor. Never run the Einstein masks on a new topic's frames merely because both videos are vertical and lavender.

Maintain source credit/rights in metadata and the archive when visible tags are removed at the user's request. Never imply ownership of the original supplied animation.

# 09 · Toolchain, implementation and practical strategies

## Tools actually used

- **Git / gh:** inspect local status and history, recover immutable source blobs, publish code through the tracked branch. GitHub operations use the configured CLI; never request credentials in chat.
- **Google Drive connector:** locate real files/folders, download source, upload master/recovery and independently verify size/MD5. Do not guess IDs from filenames.
- **Python / NumPy / OpenCV / Pillow / SciPy:** scene extraction, cleanup, source-frame interpolation, image-space depth maps, typography, audio analysis/mixing and review images.
- **imageio-ffmpeg:** obtain the working FFmpeg binary instead of assuming rendering is impossible because a system `ffmpeg` executable is missing.
- **Arena process tools:** start a long render once, record its ID, wait for completion and recover its actual state after a transport error.
- **File viewer:** inspect contact sheets and present the actual final artifact only after it exists.

The V5/V6 correction did not generate new image slides or new speech. Blender/rigged full-3D generation was not secretly used. Optional future tools must be labeled optional until they are actually installed, run and tested.

## Pinned case dependencies

The case used NumPy 2.4.6, Pillow 12.3.0, SciPy 1.17.1, imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0 and OpenCV headless 5.0.0.93. Its bundled FFmpeg reported a 7.x build. Preserve exact case requirements for reproduction; test any upgrade before calling it equivalent.

## Reusable versus historical code

`src/` contains the approved reusable policy, project compositor, generic near/far motion and output verifier. It is data-driven and contains no frozen Einstein script, voice or shot geometry. `templates/` starts empty on purpose: a new brief needs actual script/media decisions.

`projects/einstein-flow-state/versions/v5` and `v6` preserve the original implementations, timelines, selected speech, font licenses, QA and delivery identities. Running those files is historical replay, not a new production. V6's old caption renderer is retained only there; it is absent from the standard production compositor.

## Safe implementation details

Use per-project caches, not a global title cache that can leak the previous project's words. Reject unreadable type overflow, invalid timing, missing media, unsupported framing and unreviewed rights. Encode to a partial filename, verify the frame budget, then atomically expose the completed filename. A receipt must match the actual output hash before a cached render is reused.

Hashes must include relevant source, audio, timeline, profile and effect code. A filename is not sufficient cache identity. Preserve existing outputs on input changes: write a versioned output rather than silently replacing a delivered file.

## Honest support envelope

The provided generic adapter is for the tested 1080×1920 / 30fps portrait family with prepared motion clips and mixed audio. Longer scenes, other aspect ratios or RTL text require tested extensions and a storage/performance plan. It is a compositor and workflow, not a magical asset generator from an empty topic field.

## Foundation tooling corrections

The first PDF export assumed an unavailable system italic font. Documentation fonts/license are now bundled; the already licensed Barlow italic supplies the italic face. The initial inventory pass also evaluated its self-reference before first writing it; post-write existence is now rechecked. These were documentation/audit fixes only—no video, source scene or selected speech was regenerated. Further details are preserved in `records/FOUNDATION_INCIDENTS.md`.

# 10 · End-to-end production runbook

## Phase A — resume and brief

Run the repository continuity command first. Read the latest task, process ledger, delivery receipt and WF-05 policy. If work is active, execute its next step; do not create a duplicate. If an ambiguous “continue” follows a completed delivery, return/recover that verified output rather than rerendering it. Ask a targeted scope question only when no actionable work remains and the intended new change is genuinely unclear.

For a new request, open one active task and capture the visible instruction. Read `FRESH_CHAT.md`, the approved profile and the reference case. Decide whether the supplied video is a style reference or the actual content to adapt. Record topic, audience, takeaway, claims, language, format, duration, rights, voice state and delivery destination.

## Phase B — source and concept

Inspect the actual reference. Inventory available assets and previous versions before generating anything. Build a claim ledger and a semantic beat map. Select a coherent metaphor system and a fresh concept; record why alternatives were rejected. Confirm that the plan contains independent subject/layer changes, not only whole-frame zooms.

## Phase C — script and voice

Translate/write concise easy Urdu-English that retains causality and emphasis. Reuse selected audio when revising the same script. For new narration, obey the current tool's registration/selection rules; do not reuse stale session voice IDs as though they were durable audio. Save clip files/hashes and measure their real durations. Picture timing follows natural speech unless a speed change is explicitly requested.

## Phase D — shot construction

Prepare licensed/provided/native-motion or independently animated clips. Clean the old labels/social UI when adapting a flattened source, using source-specific masks. Annotate complete-subject depth plateaus and protected details. Place short integrated type into the remaining space. Choose each transition for narrative purpose. Keep the rejected lower-caption UI off.

## Phase E — prototype and full render

Build representative frames and short motion samples internally: opening, largest subject, longest headline, strongest depth transform, transition, and ending. Review them rather than asking the user to approve every trivial step. Fix real failures before the full export. Start one recorded background job; do not run long-lived work through an uncontrolled shell timeout.

Run the full encode, then inspect the encoded output—not just source frames. Repeat only the failed/changed stage with an explicit reason. Preserve successful source clips, voice and records. Do not regenerate a whole project because one title or mask failed.

## Phase F — QA and delivery

Check format/codec/frame count/faststart/full decode, audio levels, subject integrity, actual motion, typography, caption policy, tags/end card and semantic sync. Record review scope honestly. Present the existing final file. Upload it to the project's WF-05 Drive area, independently retrieve its metadata and compare size/hash. Upload a source recovery bundle and verify it too.

Update the project/registry links, checkpoint, archive the accepted small source/knowledge and only then clear the active slot. Stop the task's periodic watcher after the task is complete; do not kill a healthy production render to make a status message look tidy.

# 11 · Quality gates and acceptance

## Three separate questions

1. **Technical validity:** does the output decode, match its format and frame budget, and contain usable audio?
2. **Creative fidelity:** does it actually meet the reference/brief, preserve subjects and make the argument readable through motion?
3. **User acceptance:** does it respect the latest stated preferences, including the rejected V6 lower-caption treatment?

None implies the others. V6 passed technical checks and was delivered, yet its caption pills were later rejected. A reliable workflow records both facts instead of rewriting history as a perfect success.

## Required review dimensions

| Gate | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Correct brief/meaning | Approved script and claim ledger, not just a matching title |
| Source/rights | Real source files, attribution, rights status and hashes |
| Actual motion | Source-only temporal inspection; captions/camera alone do not prove it |
| Subject integrity | Face/hand/hair/shoe/string/prop/shadow review at entry, peak and exit |
| Typography | Readable fitted type, sensible hierarchy, no subject collision or tiny paragraph |
| Caption preference | No V6 pills/word strip in the default; plain overlay only if requested |
| Voice continuity | Matching selected files/hash; no arbitrary speed-up or wrong-topic narration |
| Semantic sync | Scene and keyword changes follow the correct spoken clauses |
| Branding | No unwanted Monarch/Instagram tags or inherited social end card |
| Export | H264 High/yuv420p, AAC stereo 48kHz, intended dimensions/FPS |
| Frame integrity | Exact frame budget, no unexpected black/missing frames, complete decode |
| Web delivery | Early moov/faststart; honest Drive processing/download fallback |
| Audio | Final decoded levels/peaks and the actual listening/content-review scope |
| Version identity | Correct output hash; not a renamed old master |
| Recovery | Full required source or verified source bundle, not only a screenshot |
| Cloud receipt | Real remote IDs; independent size/hash comparison |
| Presentation | Actual viewer success, not a planned tool call |
| Continuity | Exact next action/process status; no duplicate work or hidden restart |

This is a new operating checklist, not a retroactive claim that an old master passed a numbered set of checks that was never run.

## What the reference releases measured

V5 and V6 each had 1,893 frames, 63.1s, 1080×1920, 30fps, H264 High/yuv420p plus AAC stereo, faststart and successful full decode. Forty-two encoded samples covered fourteen shots; a separate source-motion diagnostic inspected clips before the new type. V6 verified original voice hashes and a master hash different from V5. Additional closely spaced runner frames covered a known cleanup defect.

These samples are not a mathematical proof that every pixel in every frame is flawless. Noise or a global camera move can change pixel metrics; human/agent visual interpretation still matters. Do not call RMS “LUFS,” sample peak “true peak,” or character-weighted highlighting “word-perfect speech alignment.”

## Fail closed, not indefinitely

A failed objective gate blocks delivery. A missing asset/permission or tool-required voice selection is a genuine blocker and must be named precisely. When a fix is actionable, continue working through it rather than ending with a progress promise. Preserve good work and only rerun what the changed inputs require.

---

# 12 · Continuity, persistence and zero-waste recovery

## State is not the artifact

The critical failure in V5 was not merely forgetting a sentence. A completed master, ignored runtime clips and the virtual environment disappeared after a workspace refresh while small source/receipts survived. A JSON field saying “done” did not preserve the MP4 bytes.

Protect only essential pending-upload files in a bounded snapshot-safe spool. Keep disposable caches and dependencies ignored. Respect the platform's file/patch limits. Once master and source copies are independently verified in Drive, return large media to external/ignored storage. A stable Drive ID plus hash is the durable recovery authority; do not permanently fill Git with full masters.

## Resume hierarchy

Current active task → hash-chained journal → exact resume capsule → latest checkpoint/process ledger → actual file existence/hashes → verified remote receipts → permanent style history. A condensed chat summary cannot override newer durable state.

Run `python3 tools/continuity.py resume` at every new turn. Query a recorded process before starting another. Prefer one blocking wait to repeated short polling. If a log stream disconnects, inspect process liveness, stage state, file and QA; V6 had a status-stream error even though all stages had completed successfully.

## Cache correctness

Skip a stage only when its input fingerprint, successful receipt and required artifacts all agree. Check all required scene files, not merely the last filename. An absent output invalidates a “done” receipt. A changed caption does not justify regenerating selected voice or every source object. A failed early mask does not justify abandoning the reference for new slides.

## Delivery truthfulness

Do not log “presented” before the viewer succeeds. Do not log “uploaded” before the connector returns a real ID. Do not log “synced everywhere” when only one target succeeded. Independent remote size/hash verification comes after upload. Explicitly correct a mistaken success claim in the journal.

A background Python job cannot silently perform future connector actions after the agent turn ends. The active agent must continue through QA, presentation and upload while runnable steps remain. Platform interruptions cannot be promised impossible; durable recovery can be engineered.

## Completion and repeated continue

Call the completion/archive operation while the task is still active rather than manually setting a terminal status first. The V5 archival trap is preserved as a lesson and covered by the foundation's lifecycle regression work. After delivery, a bare “continue” means check state and return the completed output—not begin the same edit again. A new explicit enhancement request starts a new version and leaves the old master intact.

Maintain a checkpoint before/after long operations, after material errors/results and at least every 55 minutes while active. The watcher supplements event checkpoints; it does not replace them. Store visible user/assistant messages accurately; do not manufacture missing compacted history or export hidden instructions/credentials.

# 13 · Version chronology and the failure-improvement chain

## Version meaning

V1/V2/V3 belong to earlier work described in the supplied conversation. V2 and V4 were later recovered and directly inspected. V3's slideshow and yuv444p/browser problem were reported in the pasted earlier transcript; the current foundation does not pretend it newly measured an unavailable V3 editing project.

V4 was visibly insufficient: original English, social tags and end card remained, and its Urdu overlay was tiny. V5 repaired the localization using actual moving source clips, restored selected natural-speed narration and per-beat scene timing, integrated Roman Urdu type, cleaned branding and a compatible export. It also forced real inspection of failed cleanup methods and persistence assumptions.

V6 was an explicitly authorized enhancement after V5 delivery. It added near/far maps, perspective/extruded titles, transition variety, highlighted lower captions and more sound accents, with a small runner cleanup repair. Its master/source were separately uploaded and verified; V5 remained intact.

The latest user feedback accepts the non-caption gains but rejects the V6 lower caption pills. That yields a permanent clean-editorial policy, not a silent rewrite of either delivered version. Both original sources and their QA/IDs remain preserved.

## Why a detailed postmortem matters

“Make it better” is not a reusable instruction by itself. Each incident needs the visible symptom, cause, correction, evidence scope and regression. The complete eighteen-lesson register follows in the codex appendix and lives in `data/lessons.json`.

The most important pattern is classification error: a still-card animation was classified as a motion match; a file receipt as preserved bytes; color as object identity; a transport timeout as failed rendering; a technical pass as user approval; and intention as tool success. The workflow now keeps these categories separate.

## What is not retroactively claimed

No newly filmed/generated 3D geometry, no new image/speech generation during the V5/V6 repair, no certified ASR word alignment, no independent human listening pass, and no guaranteed pixel-perfect restoration of obscured paper. Missing older source/scratch history is explicitly listed. Honest boundaries are part of correct production, not an excuse to lower the visual standard.

## Future improvement process

Change one clearly named component or coherent set of components. Record the user's reason, keep the previous master, update the policy only when accepted, inspect representative failure-prone frames, run the full output checks and store the new delivery identity. Do not call a changed effect “approved” merely because it is newer or more complicated.

## Additional code recovery during foundation

A 5,467-byte V3 renderer was recovered from immutable Git blob `f42b43eff8eab6d669d47681578f850a16f576e8`. Whole-scene `Image.open` inputs and absence of an explicit output yuv420p setting are now confirmed from code. The original V3 master was not newly decoded here, and its full image-asset set is not claimed available. This strengthens the documented cause without changing the evidence category of the earlier playback report.

# 14 · New-chat operating contract and response behavior

## Minimum reading order

1. Repository `AGENTS.md` and `continuity.py resume`.
2. WF-05 `FRESH_CHAT.md`, `README.md` and `data/approved-profile.json`.
3. `RESUME_STATE.md` and `data/links.json` for the latest policy and real destinations.
4. The V5 reference, accepted V6 facets and case shot map; inspect actual media when producing a new edit.
5. Relevant technical chapters and lessons before modifying that component.

Do not require the user to paste the whole history again. If the repository is not connected to a future chat, a trigger word alone cannot grant access: provide the linked hub/recovery package as the entry point. Never promise magical memory across disconnected services.

## What MOTIONGO means

For a genuine new topic/reference: resume first, establish one active task, read the current policy, inspect sources, plan the argument/metaphors, create matching narration/assets, prototype, render, QA, present, upload/verify and archive. Voice/tool-required selection or a real missing permission is a legitimate pause; trivial repeated design approval is not.

For an active revision: retain successful clips, selected speech and reference; change only the requested components. For a completed task followed by a bare continue: show the verified deliverable and clarify a new revision only if needed. Never treat a completed project as an unfinished render because a stale chat summary says otherwise.

## User-facing communication

Use concise natural Roman Urdu when replying to this user. State concrete progress, not repeated empty promises. Do not blame the user for service interruptions. Do not announce completion until the files/IDs/hashes exist. On a real blocker, say exactly which stage is blocked, what remains intact and what input/action is needed.

A completed response should lead with the actual video or requested knowledge artifact, then its viewing/download link, the material changes, the export identity and recovery status. Distinguish “2.5D/3D-style” from new 3D geometry. Do not claim browser playback was personally tested if only decoding/metadata were tested; provide a download fallback while Drive processes previews.

## Keeping the level consistent

Quality comes from repeatedly executing the brief, source inspection, metaphor logic, motion plan, hierarchy and QA—not from copying a celebratory adjective. The approved profile and tests stop specific regressions; creative review stops more subtle ones. Store every new accepted lesson in this named style so the next chat starts from accumulated evidence rather than from zero.

# 15 · Cross-platform organization and source of truth

## Roles

**Repository/GitHub:** versioned code, policy, prompts, templates, exact small source and tests. **Drive:** original reference, masters, full source/recovery bundles and readable exports. **Google Docs:** portable comprehensive human hub/codex. **Notion:** browsable project knowledge, policy callouts and the Workflows registry row. **Linear:** permanent resume pointer, finite task/acceptance status and cross-links.

The local code/policy contract and the Notion registry's discoverability role must not drift. The latest explicit user feedback overrides an old experimental preset. Link each platform to the others and to the exact same WF-05 identity. Do not rename or overwrite unrelated workflows.

## Existing folder, not a duplicate

The user-created `Wf-05 • Premium Motion Editing` folder contains the original reference and is the authority for this style's Drive organization. Add clear sections for style/playbooks, engine/templates, the Einstein case, lessons/QA, source/recovery and future projects. Preserve the original reference and old URLs. Shortcuts can organize existing masters without duplicating storage or changing their identity.

Label V5 as the clean direction reference. Label V6 as the effects reference with lower pills rejected. A novice agent must not infer that the highest version number is the preferred caption design.

## Publication transaction

Finish local source and tests → create checkpoint → publish the tracked working branch → verify remote/CI → publish or update readable hubs and source bundles → retrieve metadata/content to verify → write each target's real ID/result into its own receipt. Where the user's goal is new-chat default access, make the main-branch status explicit; an unmerged branch is not silently called main publication.

Never invent a connector ID or mark every platform complete because one upload succeeded. Keep pending/failed targets explicit. Do not collect credentials in chat or store connector tokens in the repository. Do not broaden sharing permissions merely to simplify a workflow.

## Mirrors and exact recovery

Readable mirrors link to the full canonical source rather than pretending every code file is an inline Notion paragraph. The source inventory lists each preserved case file and hash. Full media remain external by exact ID/hash; package and registry links are verified. Regenerate readable exports after policy changes so the old V6 pill instructions do not outrank the new rule.

The foundation's final coverage report states what is present, what was tested, which platforms were verified and what historical evidence was unavailable. That is the honest meaning of comprehensive: no silent gaps and no invented memories.

# 16 · Complete failure → cause → fix → regression register



## L01 · Wrong artifact type

**Symptom:** A slideshow was substituted for a motion reference.

**Root cause:** Reference dynamics were not used as an acceptance constraint.

**Correction:** Inspect dense reference frames and actual changing source; separate subject motion from camera-only zoom.

**Evidence scope:** Reported prior V3 rejection + current reference/V2/V4 inspection

**Regression/review:** No-slideshow plan and source-motion review



## L02 · Codec/browser failure

**Symptom:** An earlier V3 master reportedly used yuv444p and did not play.

**Root cause:** Encoder pixel format was not explicitly constrained.

**Correction:** H264 High/yuv420p + AAC + faststart; full decode; download fallback while Drive transcodes.

**Evidence scope:** Prior transcript report; actual V5/V6 codec checks

**Regression/review:** Codec/faststart/full-decode gates



## L03 · Tiny translated overlays

**Symptom:** V4 left English, Instagram tags/end-card and tiny Urdu text.

**Root cause:** Audio replacement plus tiny overlay was treated as localization.

**Correction:** Clean source typography/tags; rebuild readable integrated titles; replace closing card.

**Evidence scope:** Direct V4 frame review

**Regression/review:** Readable-type and tag/outro review



## L04 · Unnatural pace / scene mismatch

**Symptom:** Global speed-up forced the dub into the English video timing.

**Root cause:** Picture duration was treated as fixed instead of honoring spoken phrasing.

**Correction:** Restore selected nine clips; trim quiet only; recut each semantic shot to natural 1.0x speech.

**Evidence scope:** Recovered audio and V5/V6 code

**Regression/review:** Original voice hash and pace gates



## L05 · Cloudy cleanup

**Symptom:** Large Telea patches made cloudy paper areas.

**Root cause:** Large opaque masks and restoration method interacted badly with grain/gradient.

**Correction:** Use shot-aware glyph masks and Navier–Stokes inpainting; inspect texture, not just text absence.

**Evidence scope:** Observed rejected repair experiment

**Regression/review:** Texture inspection; no claim of perfect restoration



## L06 · Missing pale objects

**Symptom:** Color-key/background replacement damaged hair, bulbs and thin supports.

**Root cause:** Pale foreground resembled the lavender background.

**Correction:** Reject destructive keyed matte; retain full changing footage and use non-destructive near/far maps.

**Evidence scope:** Rejected matte.py + preview findings

**Regression/review:** Silhouette, hair, strings, shoes and highlight review



## L07 · Wrong tag corner

**Symptom:** Masking both possible Instagram positions cut the talent stone.

**Root cause:** Tag placement was assumed instead of detected.

**Correction:** Template-match the actually active icon corner; erase its handle only.

**Evidence scope:** Observed V5 repair; match scores approximately 0.85–0.997 vs empty 0.10–0.21

**Regression/review:** Conditional-corner test/review



## L08 · Moving heading residue

**Symptom:** Animated headings moved outside static text masks; early 1915 strokes survived.

**Root cause:** A single settled-frame rectangle was used across entry animation.

**Correction:** Use time-dependent regions and inspect entry/exit frames, not just shot midpoint.

**Evidence scope:** Observed encoded V5 correction

**Regression/review:** Dense boundary samples



## L09 · Runner feet cut / SPRINT residue

**Symptom:** Broad early lower masks cut shoes; a later ramp missed top letter strokes.

**Root cause:** Mask timing ignored the runner’s abrupt rise before the lower title entered.

**Correction:** Protect early low shoes; clean the full lower title after source t>=25.70s in this case.

**Evidence scope:** Observed V5/V6 fixes; four V6 runner samples 32.10/32.23/32.35/32.46s

**Regression/review:** Case-specific threshold, not a universal rule



## L10 · Watch/flow and flow/car leaks

**Symptom:** Approximate source boundaries showed the next subject under the wrong sentence.

**Root cause:** Sparse sampling was mistaken for exact cuts.

**Correction:** Densely inspect cuts; measured source watch end 14.97s and flow end 21.03s.

**Evidence scope:** Observed repair

**Regression/review:** Semantic EDL boundary review



## L11 · Dark bag erased

**Symptom:** Purple sandbag was classified as title ink.

**Root cause:** Color alone cannot distinguish a prop from typography.

**Correction:** Protect the large connected subject component; apply masks only in intended zones.

**Evidence scope:** Observed repair

**Regression/review:** Bag/face/limb review



## L12 · Lost export after refresh

**Symptom:** Completed ignored MP4/runtime/dependency cache disappeared before upload.

**Root cause:** Receipts persisted but ignored media bytes did not.

**Correction:** Protect a bounded pending-upload spool; verify cloud copies before returning media to ignored storage.

**Evidence scope:** Actual workspace reset; V5 recovered byte-identically

**Regression/review:** Artifact-existence + size/hash delivery gates



## L13 · Premature presentation claim

**Symptom:** A parallel log said presented although present_file failed.

**Root cause:** Intent was logged before tool success.

**Correction:** Record presentation only after success; correct the journal on failed presentation.

**Evidence scope:** Actual corrected journal

**Regression/review:** Tool-result-first receipts



## L14 · Timeout mistaken for failure

**Symptom:** V6 process-log stream disconnected after stages had completed.

**Root cause:** Transport status can differ from process/artifact status.

**Correction:** Inspect process, PIPELINE_STATE, file and QA before any restart.

**Evidence scope:** Actual V6 stream error; filesystem proved exit 0

**Regression/review:** No-duplicate execution rule



## L15 · Completion archival trap

**Symptom:** Marking checkpoint status completed before CLI complete blocked archive.

**Root cause:** complete requires an active task in the legacy controller.

**Correction:** Archive via complete while active; add regression protection for completed checkpoints.

**Evidence scope:** Actual V5 archive workaround; V6 normal completion

**Regression/review:** Continuity lifecycle regression



## L16 · Technical pass is not style approval

**Symptom:** V6 passed technical checks but user rejected its lower caption pills.

**Root cause:** Readability metrics did not encode the preferred editorial hierarchy.

**Correction:** Latest feedback overrides experiments: integrated clean type default, no pill/word strip; keep originals as history.

**Evidence scope:** Explicit user feedback 2026-10-15

**Regression/review:** Caption-policy regression tests



## L17 · Repository validation noise

**Symptom:** Ignored virtualenv binaries and a CA certificate were scanned as repository files.

**Root cause:** Filesystem enumeration did not honor ignored dependency caches.

**Correction:** Validate commit-eligible files and tracked exceptions; preserve sparse-checkout behavior.

**Evidence scope:** Observed studio.py validation failure

**Regression/review:** Manifest/cache regression test



## L18 · False completeness risk

**Symptom:** Early scratch states/full pre-init conversation or V1–V3 editable sources were not all recoverable.

**Root cause:** Compacted chat and delivered filenames are not complete source archives.

**Correction:** Separate observed/reported/proposed facts; preserve available raw source and explicitly inventory gaps.

**Evidence scope:** Evidence boundary

**Regression/review:** Coverage and provenance audit

# Einstein / Flow State — shot-by-shot source and argument map

| # | Output interval | Source interval | Concept / object | Why it works / what to protect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | 0.000–5.300s | 0.00–4.23s | Unsolved problem / tension — Oversized chalk hand + Einstein, clocks and orbital marks | Scale contrast makes cognitive pressure tangible; the hand reaches into the viewer’s space. Preserve live hand/figure/clock changes; never replace with a portrait slide. |
| 02 | 5.300–7.500s | 4.23–6.22s | Reasoning breaks down — Burning dimensional E=mc² characters | Abstract equations become vulnerable material. The formula is a visual symbol, not a proof of the gravity anecdote. |
| 03 | 7.500–10.667s | 6.22–9.65s | Time boundary and action change — Alarm clock and chalk-setting hand | 2 AM turns an abstract pause into a specific physical decision. Time shot switch to chalk/violin wording; retain full fingers and clock. |
| 04 | 10.667–17.600s | 9.65–13.72s | Change of cognitive mode — Standing violinist Einstein + expanding circular stage | Music shifts the mental frame; concentric stage is attention, not a new claim of scientific causation. Keep bow/strings/shadow, not just camera zoom. |
| 05 | 17.600–19.700s | 13.72–14.97s | Not avoidance — Hand-held pocket watch with miniature violins | Objects compress time and practice into one image. Use the short actual watch interval; avoid letting the next chaise leak into this beat. |
| 06 | 19.700–25.767s | 14.97–21.03s | Immersion versus shortcuts — Reclining violinist on a chaise, hovering cursor arrows | Digital pointers intrude on a human practice state. Type FLOW STATE then AI SHORTCUTS follows argument; not constant subtitle clutter. |
| 07 | 25.767–29.867s | 21.03–23.80s | Convenience / speed — Violet striped car in changing perspective | Fast transport introduces a familiar tool-benefit premise. The car must change orientation/position in source footage, not be a still card. |
| 08 | 29.867–34.067s | 23.80–27.13s | Chosen effort — Runner, orbit and changing stride | People still train despite owning machines. Protect every shoe/leg frame while cleaning old labels; motion serves contrast with car. |
| 09 | 34.067–38.533s | 27.13–30.63s | Outsourced work — Motorcycle with engine-headed passenger | Effort transferred to a machine becomes visible. Do not equate body shape with worth or treat the metaphor as medical evidence. |
| 10 | 38.533–40.400s | 30.63–32.20s | Mental practice analogy — Bandaged brain supported by crutches | The argument makes disuse visible through a fragile support structure. Retain pale bandage and thin crutches; disability imagery is metaphor, not diagnosis. |
| 11 | 40.400–45.667s | 32.20–36.23s | Effort replaced — Laptop suspended from bulb balloons + deflated bulb | Ideas appear inflated while the difficult climb is absent. Retain strings, screen and pale bulb highlights; the exact phrase is rhetorical. |
| 12 | 45.667–49.467s | 36.23–39.70s | Divergent measures — Rising bulbs versus brain tied to a stone | Opposing vertical vectors show efficiency up / talent down. Mask only the active tag corner: the stone occupies the other corner. |
| 13 | 49.467–56.767s | 39.70–46.30s | Paid resistance — Runner carrying a heavy bag in an empty stadium argument | Voluntary difficulty converts an apparently irrational action into training. Protect dark-purple bag from being mistaken for heading ink; articulate weight. |
| 14 | 56.767–63.100s | 46.30–51.64s | Unresolved consequence — Two rows of pen nibs | The tool-of-art becomes the closing object and open question. End in clean editorial space, not the source Instagram card. |

Counts: 14 shots; 9 selected speech clips; 31 integrated title states; 36 phrase segments; 1,893 output frames at 30 fps; 63.1 seconds. Source interval ends at 51.64s, excluding the original social end card.

Exact clip trims, title timing, type sizes and phrase text remain in each version’s `timeline.json` and `prepare_audio.py`. The standard profile disables the separate V6 lower caption UI, not the integrated lower-third headline positions.

## Evidence boundaries

# Evidence scope and honest completeness

This foundation consolidates all available V5/V6 source, selected speech, fonts/licenses, timelines, measured QA, delivery receipts, preserved visible-chat/journal records, and the explicit 2026-10-15 feedback. Each copied case file is inventoried by hash. No master is silently replaced.

## Boundaries

- Full pre-initialization / compacted chat cannot be recreated verbatim. The large pasted prior-agent transcript was not saved in full during V5; excerpts and the recorded decisions are preserved.
- V1/V2 editable project sources were not recovered. V2 and V4 videos were directly inspected in the repair; V3 slideshow/codec failures were reported in the supplied earlier transcript. Do not promote a reported observation into a newly measured result.
- Temporary contact sheets and some early scratch-state bytes were lost in workspace resets. Their observations are recorded; current source can regenerate current reviews, not certify missing historical pixels byte-for-byte.
- V5 and V6 are reference-derived edits. Original source credit remains @RIT2RAJ_DAS. Neither is a newly modeled 3D film.
- Existing voice clips are the spoken authority. Roman Urdu phrase text is the on-screen script, not a certified word-exact ASR transcript.
- V5/V6 full decode, codec, hash and sampled-frame checks are measured. An independent human listening pass was not claimed.
- A technical QA pass did not equal aesthetic approval: the user later rejected V6 bottom caption pills.
- The approved combined policy is reusable configuration/code. No newly rendered full-length hybrid master is claimed by this documentation task.
